key_insight: In Sr1−xNdxCoO3−δ, adding oxygen triggers a structural shift from layered I4/mmm to oxygen-deficient Pmmm and simultaneously drives a magnetic/transport transition from antiferromagnetic, resistive behavior to ferromagnetic, low-resistance behavior.
engineering_relevance: Oxygen vacancy control emerges as a practical tuning knob for tailoring cobalt-perovskite phase stability, magnetism, and conductivity in oxide-functional materials.
method: Magnetic and electrotransport measurements across x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct structural refinement plus correlated magnetic and resistivity trends showing oxygen-content-driven phase evolution and a drastic resistivity decrease.
watch_item: The ferromagnetic state is described as magnetically inhomogeneous and vacancy-influenced, so device behavior may depend sensitively on oxygen stoichiometry and defect ordering.
